question: Which durable memory-core dreaming resource-control API should OpenClaw accept for this issue: a plugin-level agent allowlist, per-agent dreaming overrides and schedules, or pressure/stagger behavior instead of explicit scoping?
rationale: Repository policy treats config surface as compatibility-sensitive, and the issue discussion plus open PRs propose different shapes with different upgrade and operator tradeoffs.

options.title: Adopt plugin-level allowlist first
options.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057 or an equivalent plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.agents implementation, then track schedules separately.

options.title: Require per-agent overrides
options.body: Ask for agents.list[].dreaming or agents.list[].memory.extensions.memory-core.dreaming with explicit schedule semantics before accepting a fix, which is broader but matches the original request more closely.

options.title: Defer to pressure/backoff work
options.body: Prioritize https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84848 and leave explicit per-agent scoping undecided, which may reduce overload but leaves the durable opt-out use case open.

recommendation.title: Adopt plugin-level allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review and land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100057 or an equivalent plugins.entries.memory-core.config.dreaming.agents implementation, then track schedules separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and prior memory-core dreaming history make this the strongest available owner for the config/runtime boundary choice.
